blocks.text: Deduplicate siblings, not all depths

Because the input is sorted, equal values are adjacent. At one combination depth, indices start, start + 1, ... are sibling candidates for the same path prefix. The first occurrence of a value represents that value choice.

If i > start and candidates[i] equals candidates[i - 1], the earlier equal value was already available as a sibling and produces the same value-level subtree, so the later sibling is skipped. In a child call start changes; i may then equal the new start, allowing another physical copy at a deeper result position.

Equal values may be legal at different depths when multiplicity permits. The first occurrence should represent the value choice at this depth. This can incorrectly remove a legal repeated value at a deeper level.

Visited or used state answers whether this exact index, node, or cell may be used again on the active path. It prevents illegal resource reuse even when every value is distinct.

blocks.text: Separate generation cost from retained unique output
The implementation deliberately visits all n! indexed leaves. At each leaf it copies n values and hashes or compares a length-n key, so generation-and-copy work is O(n · n!).

After deduplication, only u value-distinct paths remain, each with n stored values. The final output payload therefore uses O(un) space, excluding transient recursion state and hash-table overhead of lower order relative to stored keys.
